turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Nora's in the chair whenever you're ready. I've the obs done, she's a bit warm. Parking was a nightmare, just so you know.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Grand. Nora, you look wrecked. What's brought you in?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): The face of me. It's swelled up and the tooth is throbbing. I'm after a crown and I'm destroyed with it.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which side, and when did the crown go on?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Left. And I'm not sleeping with it, it's just... ugh.
[SEG0006] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Sorry doctor. The crown was Thursday, so that's three days. The dentist is away till next week, that's why I brought her.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Three days of this on the left. Throbbing, worse at night. I can't even lie on it.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any temperature with it?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm roasting in the bed. Umm. A bit of a fever, nothing mad.
[SEG0010] person_1 (NURSE): Temp is 37.8, pulse ninety four, pressure 136 over 84, sats 98 percent. Respirations 16.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Open a small bit... the left cheek is warm, swollen, tender along the jaw. No obvious collection I can feel. Mouth opening is a bit tight.
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah will you stop. That hurts. Don't be poking at it.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry. Any trouble swallowing your spit or your food?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Swallowing is grand.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the breathing, any tightness or...
[SEG0016] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She was up half the night pacing. I nearly rang the out of hours, I didn't know whether...
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Breathing is fine. Not a bother. I'm wrecked and cranky, leave the pacing out of it.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair enough. What have you had for the pain?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Paracetamol from the chemist. Two tablets. Doesn't touch it.
[SEG0020] person_4 (CAREGIVER): It's a gram, four times a day, I set them out. She missed the lunchtime one yesterday, and I'm not sure she took the evening one, she was dozing.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other regular tablets?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): The sugar ones. I forget the... err. The name of them.
[SEG0023] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Metformin. Five hundred milligrams twice a day, for the diabetes. She's been on it years.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so the diabetes is ongoing. Anything else in the gut, or with the waterworks?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. Can we get to the tooth.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking amoxacillin, five hundred three times a day for five days, and I'll see you in a fortnight. That should cover it.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Hang on, penicillin. I can't have penicillin.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): What happened when you had it?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Years ago, for a chest thing. A rash all over me and my lips swelled up. They told me never again.
[SEG0030] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The lips were bad that time. She's stayed away from it since.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, scrap that. No amoxicillin, nothing in that family. We'll use clindamicyn, three hundred milligrams four times a day for five days, by mouth.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Four times. I'm tired just hearing it.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): I know. And a fortnight is wrong as well, err, now I'm thinking about the diabetes and the fever and the cheek still coming up.
[SEG0034] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She's been a bit higher on the sugars the last day or two too.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): That settles it. Nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, a full blood count and a CRP. No fasting, you can eat, just come at half eight.
[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): Thursday half eight is free. I'll book her in.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): And I'll see you here Friday morning, not in two weeks. We'll look at the swelling and the bloods.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Friday. More waiting. That telly outside is brutal, cookery on a loop.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the swelling hasn't settled by Friday, or if you're worse, then we do a scan of the face. Not booking it now. If those bloods are borderline I'll add a swab of the gum, only if they're borderline.
[SEG0040] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And if she goes downhill before Friday?
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): If swallowing gets hard, or the breathing gets difficult, or the swelling runs to the eye or down the neck, straight to the emergency department. Don't wait for me.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): I hear you. I'm not deaf. I'm sore and I want the bed.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Soft food only. Keep the paracetamol going the way it's set out, and finish every dose of the clindamycin even when the tooth eases. Ring the dentist when they're back next week.
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Right. Fine.
[SEG0045] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Will the tablet fix the crown, or is the tooth gone?

[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Working read, it's an infection under the crown, a dental abscess, and the antibiotic should knock it back. Could also be cellulitis of the cheek without a pocket of pus, I can't separate those fully today. Prescription is at reception, Thursday half eight for the bloods, Friday morning with me.

spec.situation: Cheek swelling and throbbing toothache for three days after a crown; fever mild; dentist unavailable; doctor prescribes antibiotic, warns about swallowing or breathing difficulty.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

omissions.text: Paracetamol was reported as not relieving the pain ('doesn't touch it').
The doctor initially planned amoxicillin 500 mg three times a day for 5 days, then changed this plan after the penicillin allergy was disclosed.
Penicillin allergy severity/detail was reinforced by caregiver: lip swelling was 'bad that time' and she has avoided penicillin since.
Follow-up timing was explicitly corrected: not in two weeks/fortnight, but Friday morning instead because of diabetes, fever, and ongoing cheek swelling.
